name: coverage levels are per source: one source fully covered does not make the claim fully covered
notes: §6.1 v1.4: with several relevant sources, coverage levels are per source: full iff every relevant source is full, none iff every one is none, else partial. The patch gives email.sent two sources (gmail.sent, gcal.event) and drops partial_coverage, so a partial claim falls to the terminal default_unverifiable, which adds no rule code: the per-source level decides the outcome without any per-source reason (how many coverage.partial reasons a two-source claim carries is left open, README).
The grant binds acct-a for both sources (no account_unbound, no cap); the gcal.event entry has allCalendars. Both entries synced 17:00 = evaluatedAt. No observations.

c1 (14:02): window [14:00, 14:48]. gmail.sent [12:00, 17:00] contains it → full; gcal.event [12:00, 15:00] contains it → full. Combined full. graceElapsed: each source has a sync ≥ end + 30 and ≥ end + 45 (14:48). No candidate → not_found → NOT_FOUND, FINAL, reasons match.none (accounts bound, so no coverage.account_unbound).

c2 (16:02): window [16:00, 16:48]. gmail.sent full; gcal.event's interval ends at 15:00 → none. Per source → partial. graceElapsed true (both synced 17:00 ≥ 16:48). No rule matches (not_found needs full, pending needs grace not elapsed) → default_unverifiable → UNVERIFIABLE, reasons match.none. PENDING (§8): 17:00 < end(16:03) + 24 h.
Reading coverage as the union of every relevant interval would call c2 full ([12:00, 17:00] ⊇ [16:00, 16:48]) and give a false NOT_FOUND (Hard Rule 5).
